page.title: Best 2000Wh Power Station (2026): tested picks for home, RV and camping
page.desc: The best 2000Wh power station for most buyers, with today's prices, weights, solar input and 30-amp RV outlets compared across Growatt, EcoFlow, BLUETTI, Jackery and Anker.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 2000Wh power station is the Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO ({buy:growatt-infinity-2000-pro}): 2,048 Wh and 2,400 W for less than the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 or Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 cost today, with 1,200 W of solar input and a 30-amp TT-30 RV outlet that none of those three have. The main worry with Growatt is support, not the hardware: its product page says 5 years of warranty while its policy page says 2, and one of the three reviews on its own store describes a stalled warranty claim, so register it in the MyGro app within 30 days and keep the receipt. If you need the lightest 2 kWh unit, the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at about 40 lb beats the 51-lb Growatt, but it takes only 400 W of solar and costs more.

All five units here use LiFePO4 cells rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles, so the real differences are price, weight, how fast they recharge from sun and whether an RV can plug in directly. Prices were read on each maker's US store on 2026-11-06.
page.after:
What owners complain about

Across the reviews and owner comments we read, the same five issues come up for 2 kWh stations, and the Growatt is not immune to any of them.

  • Fan noise under load. Every tester who ran the INFINITY 2000 or 2000 PRO above about 1,500 W heard the fan, and one measured 45 dB at 3 ft. Quiet-charge mode cuts AC input to roughly 400 W to keep it silent at night.
  • App pairing. Three reviewers had the MyGro app fail to find the unit the first time; toggling Bluetooth and Wi-Fi fixed it. The runtime estimate is rough and one owner needed a full charge cycle to recalibrate the percentage.
  • Warranty follow-through. Growatt's own store carries a one-star review about an approved claim with no replacement sent, and Trustpilot reviews of the parent company are split between fast fixes and unanswered emails. Buy from the store, register within 30 days and keep the invoice.
  • Weight. At about 51 lb with no wheels the Growatt, like the 53-lb BLUETTI, is a two-hand carry. Only the Jackery and Anker drop near 40 lb.
  • Returns. Lithium units are often non-returnable on marketplaces. Growatt's store allows 30 days but you pay return freight and about 5%.

Which one by need

  • Most battery for the money, or RV hookup: Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO ({buy:growatt-infinity-2000-pro}). It was the cheapest in-stock 2 kWh unit from these brands on 2026-11-06, takes 1,200 W of solar, and its TT-30 lets a 30-amp RV cord plug straight in. The BLUETTI AC200L also has a TT-30 but was out of stock on BLUETTI's store the same day.
  • Lightest to carry: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at about 40 lb. Accept 400 W of solar, three AC outlets and no expansion.
  • Quiet desk UPS: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, with a 10 ms switchover and 25 dB at a 600 W load in one test. No TT-30 and no expansion on the base model.
  • Highest continuous output in the class: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ({buy:bluetti-elite-200-v2}) at 2,600 W, charged to full in 1.4 hours, with a 5-year warranty.
  • Whole-house or 240 V loads: step up to the Growatt HELIOS 3600 ({buy:growatt-helios-3600}): 3,686 Wh, 3,600 W, charges in about 1.5 hours from a 240 V outlet, and two units with Growatt's hub give 240 V / 7,200 W.

Not recommended

  • Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 at its current store price. Good hardware at 41.7 lb, but it cost $400 more than the Growatt on 2026-11-06 for the same capacity and only 800 W of solar input. It is worth a look only when discounted.
  • Any 2 kWh unit for a 13,500 BTU rooftop air conditioner. A TT-30 outlet does not change the 2,400 W inverter limit or the roughly 2 kWh you have to spend; expect an hour or two of A/C, not an afternoon.
